key_insight: AtomWorld-Mirror replaces event-by-event atomistic simulation with a time-aware macro-step world model that predicts physically reachable state changes and elapsed time for long-horizon materials evolution.
engineering_relevance: This could enable much faster simulation of diffusion, damage, and fracture-related processes while preserving structural validity, making long-time materials design and reliability studies more practical.
method: Distills short micro-event segments into latent macro-step transitions between key atomic states.
Jointly predicts sparse structural edits and accumulated physical time.
Uses reachability, inventory conservation, and continuous-time consistency constraints to enforce physical plausibility.
evidence_signal: Across five atomic systems, including Cu-rich RPV steel irradiation aging, Cu-Zr metallic glass, and Li3N-based anti-perovskite solid electrolyte, the method reports 10^3 to 10^4× speedups over event-by-event simulation.
watch_item: Macro-step predictions may be sensitive to how well the latent model generalizes to unseen chemistries, defect pathways, or loading conditions beyond the training regimes.
paper_title: AtomWorld-Mirror: Macro-Step World Modeling of Critical Evolution Backbones for Materials Dynamics
